summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and a cough. The chest pain occurred both with coughing and exertion. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction, with normal cardiac enzymes and a normal exercise stress MIBI test. The cough was attributed to acute bronchitis, with improvement after IV fluids. A dental Panorex revealed radiolucency at tooth #21, concerning for infection, and the patient was started on penicillin. Chronic conditions including coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and diastolic heart failure were managed with medication adjustments. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with dentistry and monitor weight and symptoms.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Acute apical periodontitis of pulpal origin
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
